parts.title: Multiple choice (Questions 1–50)
parts.instructions: This paper has 50 multiple-choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose ONE best answer and blacken its letter on the separate answer sheet. Sections: A. Dialogue (1–4), B. Grammar and vocabulary (5–34), C. Table (35–40), D. Reading passage (41–50).

Bold words in stems are plain text; no underlining. V-B has the same questions, reordered, with options shuffled.

passages.title: Dialogue between a father and a son cooking in the kitchen
passages.instructions: Complete the dialogue between a father and a son cooking in the kitchen. Choose the father’s correct answers from the choices given (A–D).
paragraphs: Son: What shall I do now?
Son: How much water should I put in?
Son: But why all these? Should I add any salt?
Son: How long should I wait?
Choices given: A. Five to ten minutes.  B. Two or three cups.  C. Can you heat the water while I chop the onions?  D. No. Wait for a moment.

passages.title: Table: four countries
passages.instructions: Answer questions 35–40 according to the information in the table.

passages.title: The foolish husband and wife
passages.instructions: Read the story and answer the questions (41–50) according to the information in the story.
paragraphs: Long time ago a man and his wife lived in a village. They had many chickens and goats. One day they wanted to eat chicken for their lunch. So they killed two of their chickens and cooked them in a big pot. Then they went to the river to bring water.

On their way, they met three young men. “You three!” called the husband. “We have [line 5] cooked chicken at home. Our house is near that big tree. The chicken is in a big pot. The door is locked and the key is under a stone below the window. Please don’t eat it.”

“No, no. We will not do that,” the three men promised. But after the husband and the wife left, they went to the house immediately. They took the key and opened the door. They found the pot full of chicken and ate it quickly. After they had finished, they closed [line 10] the pot, locked the door and put the key under the stone below the window and ran away.

After some time, the husband and the wife returned to their home. They took the key and opened the door. When they opened the pot, the chicken meat was not there. “Where is our chicken? Where is our chicken?” they shouted.

In the pot there were a lot of flies only. The husband and his wife thought that the flies [line 15] had eaten their chicken. They were very angry. There were many flies everywhere in the house. Then they started to kill the flies. A fly sat on the woman’s head. “Kill the fly,” said the woman quietly pointing to the fly on her head. The man took an axe, saw the fly on his wife’s head and tried to kill it. He hit her on the head with the axe and she died. But the fly flew away!
passages.note: The paper gives no title. Line numbers (5, 10, 15) as printed.

questions.stem: Dialogue, gap (1). Son: “What shall I do now?” Father: “______” Son: “How much water should I put in?”

questions.stem: I was born ______ May, 1992.
explanation_steps: Month and year (no day) → in: in May 1992.

questions.stem: As plough is to farmer, ______ is to footballer.
explanation_steps: A farmer works with a plough; a footballer’s work is to play football.
Of the four words only “play” belongs to a footballer.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Appendix 1: Vocabulary list, p. 221–227.
tips: Find the word that belongs to the second person.

similar_questions.stem: As pen is to writer, ______ is to farmer.
explanation_steps: tool of a farmer.

textbook_ref.rule: Read the whole sentence: the words before and after tell you the meaning of the new word.

questions.review_flag: Faulty analogy: plough is a TOOL (noun) but all four options are verbs; the tool of a footballer (ball) is not offered. C ‘play’ is the only option linked to a footballer.

questions.stem: When the teacher ______ in, the students were studying.
explanation_steps: Past continuous (were studying) + a short past action → past simple: came.
Textbook: English Grade 7, p. 72; English Grade 8, p. 7.
tips: When + past simple, … was/were + -ing.

similar_questions.stem: When I ______ home, my mother was cooking.
explanation_steps: arrived.

textbook_ref.rule: Past simple: verb-ed or irregular past form; questions and negatives use did + base verb (Did he call?).
textbook_ref.note: textbook: English Grade 7, p. 72; English Grade 8, p. 7

additional_textbook_refs.rule: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing; it shows an action that was going on at a time in the past.

questions.stem: Which of the following has correct spelling?

questions.stem: ______ he came on time, he didn’t catch the bus.

similar_questions.stem: ______ she was tired, she finished the work.

questions.stem: In which order would the following words be written in a dictionary?

last vs law: third letters s and w → last first.

questions.stem: A farmer is someone ______ plants trees.

questions.stem: She ______ by her teacher to study hard.

questions.stem: His uncle said, “We are late.” The correct indirect speech is:

options.A: He said that you are late.
options.B: He said that we are late.
options.C: He said that they were late.
options.D: He said that they are late.

are → were.

similar_questions.stem: The girls said, “We are hungry.” Indirect:

options.A: They said that they were hungry.
options.C: They said that you were hungry.

questions.stem: She likes ______ pictures.

options.D: Russia has the largest population of all.

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is false about Brazil?

options.A: It has larger population than Canada.

A, B, D are true.

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is true?

options.A: Russia is bigger than China in area. But is it hotter than Canada.
options.B: Brazil has smaller population than Russia. It is the coldest of all.
options.C: China has the largest population. But it is colder than Canada.
options.D: Canada has smaller population than Brazil. But it is hotter than Russia.

explanation_steps: D: Canada 35 < Brazil 200 (true) and Canada 9 °C > Russia 7 °C (true) → D true.
A: second part false (7 °C is colder than 9 °C). B and C are false.
Textbook: English Grade 8, Unit 6 (p. 120–141): graphs and data.
questions.explain_simple: Canada has fewer people than Brazil and is hotter than Russia (9 > 7).
tips: Both sentences in the option must be true.

options.A: China is hotter than Brazil. It has the most people.

explanation_steps: 29 > 25 and 1321 million.

questions.stem: Which of the following is false?

options.A: The husband and the wife did not eat the chicken.
options.B: The husband, the wife and the men ate the chicken.
options.C: The three young men ate the chicken.

explanation_steps: Only the three young men ate the chicken. The husband and wife found the pot empty.
So B is false. A and C are true.
Textbook: English Grade 8, reading lessons.
questions.explain_simple: Only the young men ate it. B is false.
